title: Runlet DSL Bridge: lightweight runbook-as-task SDK and admin gadget set
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Oncall and support engineers rely on ad-hoc scripts and long prose runbooks. Those artifacts are brittle, hard to test, and often require interactive steps. We need a compact, typed DSL + minimal SDK that lets engineers author runbooks-as-tasks ("runlets") that are:
acceptance_criteria: 1) Authors can write a runlet in TypeScript or Python that composes primitive admin helpers (e.g., 'query-deployments', 'evict-node', 'rotate-key') and publish it to the ops catalog; 2) Runlets can be executed via CLI, Console button, or API with role-based authorization and an auditable event emitted for every step; 3) Dry-run mode returns a deterministic plan without side effects; 4) Built-in safety gates (requires confirm for destructive steps, automatic retry/backoff, idempotency checks) are plumbed and enabled by default; 5) Telemetry hooks emit step-level timing, success/failure codes, and per-runlet run_id to the ops dashboard; 6) Library ships with 10 canonical runlets (restart service, rotate credentials, failover-region) and 80% unit test coverage for core SDK functions.
description_details: Scope: - SDK core: minimal runtime that provides typed inputs/outputs, step composition, scoped secrets access, and sandboxed helpers. - Bridge service: small control-plane service that validates runlets, stores metadata, enforces RBAC, and provides execution tokens. - Console integration: a one-click 'Run' affordance and execution log viewer. - CLI integration: local dev run and remote execution driver. - Safety & audit: confirm flows, escrowed escalation for high-risk actions, and append-only audit events to customer audit log when running in Dedicated/Private. Out of scope: full graphical workflow builder (follow-up), complex long-lived human approval flows (phase 2).
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed - prototype DSL is a tiny wrapper around async generator steps; validated we can intercept steps for dry-run and telemetry.
2026-02-20: Design sync with Console team - determined minimal UI surface: runlet details page, run history, and 'Run (dry/run)' modal. PM asked for explicit RBAC mapping to existing role groups.
2026-02-28: Security review kickoff - threat model doc uploaded; notable requirement: short-lived exec tokens and KMS-backed secret fetch with least privilege.
2026-03-05: Implemented initial CLI invoke and remote-exec API; smoke tests show runlet dry-run returns plan in <200ms for simple runlets.
2026-03-11: Added step-level telemetry prototype; emitted events visible in ops dashboard for a sample restart-service runlet.
2026-03-14: Began unit test authoring and wired gRPC shim for Bridge service; still blocked on deploy IAM policy for staging cluster.
comments: PM (Rosa Gomez): Please ensure the catalog UI surfaces mitigation steps and expected blast radius clearly. Don't ship with ambiguous step names.
Design (Elliot Park): Suggest a compact step UI that collapses low-risk steps and surfaces high-risk confirmation prominently.
Security (Tariq Mahmood): Exec tokens must expire <= 5 minutes and be scope-limited to only the runlet-id and requested permissions.
Eng (Nora Kim): Suggest keeping the SDK unobtrusive — core helpers only; avoid large runtime dependencies to ease on-prem packaging.
Reviewer (Julian Rivera): Look at our incident from 2025-09 when a scripted DB failover lacked dry-run; add regression tests that exercise destructive flags.
decisions: Use a generator-based step API to provide stable dry-run and replay semantics.
Implement Bridge as a single small control-plane service (Go) to ease on-prem cross-compilation and low memory footprint.
Default runlets to 'safe-mode' where destructive helpers require explicit confirm parameter or escalation token.
tradeoffs: We could have chosen a full YAML workflow format (more authorable for non-devs) but chose an SDK-first approach to keep the primitives typed, testable, and packageable into existing code repos. This raises the initial bar for authors (developer-centric) but shortens iteration cycles and supports unit tests.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): Deploy Bridge to staging, enable runlets for internal SRE team only; collect telemetry for 72 hours.
Phase 1 (beta): Expose CLI + Console button to engineering oncall rotation; require opt-in via team whitelist; monitor audit trails and incident postmortems.
Phase 2 (GA): Open to all internal teams, add analytics surface in Console (successful runs, mean time, failure rates), and ship on-prem package for Private customers.
Rollback: Bridge includes toggle to disable remote-exec while preserving catalog read-only; CLI will still allow local dev dry-runs.
qa_checks: Unit tests: 80% coverage for SDK core (step composition, dry-run, idempotency).
E2E: run Bridge + Console smoke that executes a non-destructive runlet end-to-end with telemetry verified in dashboard.
Security: token expiry and scope tests; secret-fetch respects IAM and KMS error modes.
Chaos: simulate Bridge restart mid-execution and verify runlets either resume or abort cleanly with clear status.
tasks: SDK: author core step runtime + dry-run mode (Liam) - 3 points
Bridge service: validation, signing, exec tokens (Marta) - 3 points
Console: run modal and log viewer (Design + Console eng) - 2 points
CLI: dev run and remote driver (TBD) - 2 points
Tests: unit + e2e harness and chaos scenarios (QA) - 2 points
Docs: PRD -> README and cookbook runlets (DX) - 1 point
risk_mitigation: Enforce safe-mode defaults and require explicit 'confirm=true' for high-risk helpers.
Escalation workflow for unavailable Bridge: fallback to local dry-run only; remote-exec disabled.
Audit events are append-only and replicated to the central audit log (Dedicated/Private) to prevent tampering.
